The pore sizes 2.4, 5.0, 9.5, and 9.6 nm are explicitly stated in the text (Section 3.1) and listed in Table 1. However, the extracted BET surface area value of 455 m2 g−1 is not a general BET value for the set; it corresponds specifically to Sample 2 (pore size 5.0 nm) in Table 1. Table 1 lists BET surface areas as 368 (2.4 nm), 455 (5.0 nm), 421 (9.5 nm), and 367 (9.6 nm). Therefore, returning only 455 m2 g−1 alongside multiple pore sizes is incomplete/misleading for the field as extracted. Fig. 1 is about pore size distribution and does not provide BET area values.
entity_reviews.llm_suggested_fix: Either (a) report BET surface areas for each pore size: 368 (2.4 nm), 455 (5.0 nm), 421 (9.5 nm), 367 (9.6 nm) m2 g−1 (Table 1), or (b) if only one BET value is needed, tie 455 m2 g−1 explicitly to the 5.0 nm sample only.

entity_reviews.llm_reasoning: The paper explicitly states in the XRD section (Fig. 4(a) discussion) that the crystallite size of Li2ZnI4 in the composite was estimated to be 20 nm using Scherrer's equation. This directly supports the extracted crystallite_size = 20 nm for XRD (Cu Kα).

The paper explicitly reports three 6Li MAS-NMR chemical shifts: a peak at −4.9 ppm for pure Li2ZnI4 (and also pure LiI), plus additional environments at −0.8 ppm and −2.8 ppm in the composites. This is stated in the Abstract (Page 1) and repeated in the Results section with Fig. 5 description (Page 4: “A single peak at −4.9 ppm... additional lithium ion environment at −0.8 ppm and −2.8 ppm...”). The alleged provenance “Fig. 5” is consistent with the text around Fig. 5.

The paper explicitly reports that in the 6Li CP/MAS-NMR measurement of the composite, a single peak at −0.8 ppm was observed (text in Results/Discussion: “A single peak at −0.8 ppm (Fig. 6(b)) was observed for the CP/MAS measurement of the composite.”). This supports the extracted chemical shift value −0.8 ppm for 6Li CP MAS-NMR, and the alleged provenance Fig. 6(b) matches the described result.

The paper explicitly states that the maximum conductivity of the Li2ZnI4–mesoporous-Al2O3 composite is “more than fifty times higher than that of pure Li2ZnI4” (Results 3.2 and caption/text for Fig. 3(a)/(b)). The abstract and conclusions also reiterate “More than fifty times enhancement of the electrical conductivity…”. This supports an increase factor of 50 (at least 50×).
